messages:
Amanda: starting warroom for multiple customer reports of 5xx/timeouts on /v1/chat/streaming at 03:14 UTC, grouping as one incident. seeing ~12% p50->p99 spike, some 504s and 502s. @Jesse can you confirm scope?
Jesse: confirmed. affects eu-west and us-central streaming endpoints, mostly function-calling flows. spike started ~03:08. small subset of clients, but high error-rate for those flows. reproducing locally now.
Pranav: signal shows auth-proxy upstream returning 502s followed by gateway 504s. connection pools hitting max. logs: `auth-proxy: 502 upstream reset` then `apigw: connpool_exhausted`.
Li: interesting — telemetry shows a burst of token refresh requests at the same time, ~3k/s, most from the streaming route. looks like token cache missed.
Sofia: customer support reports timeouts and failed streams, a few billing alerts fired (auth failures bubbling to credit-check code). support-bot: escalations queued: ACME Corp, SparkChat, NovaApps.
Tom: deploy-bot: canary for auth-refresh v2 rolled at 02:50 UTC to 10% of traffic. rolled back at 02:58 for unrelated metrics but maybe partial windows remained.
Amanda: hypothesis: token-refresh canary caused per-request refresh instead of cached tokens -> thundering refreshes -> auth-proxy saturation -> conn pool exhaustion -> gateway 5xx/504.
Jesse: repro steps I'm running: 1) open streaming chat with function call 2) intentionally short-lived tokens 3) rapid reconnects. I can reproduce 502s in staging with canary enabled.
Pranav: grep from prod edge (snippet):
```
2026-03-18T03:09:12Z auth-proxy[pid=2345]: refresh_request id=xx client=acme seq=341 token_cache_miss
2026-03-18T03:09:12Z auth-proxy[pid=2345]: upstream_error 502 reset
2026-03-18T03:09:12Z apigw[pid=678]: connpool_exhausted route=/v1/chat/streaming
```
Li: also seeing many short lived TCP sessions (FIN soon after SYN) — clients retrying quickly. keepalive settings may be exacerbating.
Sofia: immediate customer comms: posting in support threads that we have a platform incident and working on mitigation. customers notified with status page update.
Amanda: mitigation plan (short): 1) rollback any lingering canary traffic -> Jesse/Tom, 2) temporarily raise auth-proxy conn pool limit and connection timeout -> Pranav/Li, 3) enable token-cache fallback in apigw (cache on edge) -> Tom, 4) apply per-customer concurrency throttle for streaming -> Sofia ops/UI.
Jesse: rolling canary rollback now (cmd: `kubectl patch deploy auth-refresh --replicas=0 --namespace=canary`) — patch applied.
deploy-bot: deploy event: auth-refresh canary scale-down initiated by Jesse at 03:20 UTC. status: scaled to 0 replicas.
Pranav: bumping proxy pool: `env AUTH_PROXY_MAX_CONN=1200` applied to auth-proxy in eu-west. scaling auth-proxy to 3->5 pods.
Li: increased keepalive timeout from 30s -> 90s on edge NLB to reduce churn.
Tom: enabling edge token-cache fallback (experimental): toggled `EDGE_TOKEN_CACHE=true` for rolling 60s window. will monitor cache hit rate.
Sofia: applied temporary per-customer concurrent streaming limit = 8 to reduce fanout. support-bot: updated affected customers list.
Amanda: monitoring: p50 latency down, p95 improving, error-rate dropped from 12% -> 2% in eu-west in next 6m.
Jesse: staging repro gone when canary disabled. good sign.
Pranav: auth-proxy error-rate down to baseline, but we saw a secondary spike when cache TTL expired for some clients. need better cache warmup.
Li: note: some clients (mobile SDK v1.2.0) reconnect aggressively when they see partial frames. SDK team flagged.
Sofia: comms update: customers notified that mitigations in place, follow-up postmortem promised. reactions: :thumbsup: from ACME.
Amanda: OK moving to postmortem/next steps. Capture root cause, timeline, mitigations, and action items. quick notes: root cause = canary token-refresh behavior + token-cache miss + aggressive client reconnects -> auth-proxy connection exhaustion -> gateway 5xx/timeouts.
Jesse: timeline (short): 02:50 canary roll, 03:08 spike begins, 03:20 rollback and mitigations, 03:30 error-rate near baseline.
Pranav: short-term action items (owners):
- (Pranav) Add alert for token-refresh-rate anomaly and auth-proxy connpool saturation threshold (ETA: 48h)
- (Tom) Harden token-cache warmup and increase default TTL for edge cache (ETA: 72h)
- (Jesse) Add canary kill-switch automation so canary traffic drains faster on rollback (ETA: 1 week)
- (Li) Tune NLB keepalive defaults and add metrics for short-live TCP sessions (ETA: 72h)
- (Sofia) Customer comms follow-up and case owners list (ETA: 24h)
- (Amanda) Postmortem doc + retro (owners: Amanda/Jesse) (ETA: 72h)

Amanda: long-term mitigations:
- token refresh design change: central refresh queue to avoid per-request refresh
- improved per-customer backpressure in runtime and SDK guidance
- stronger canary gating (load tests + token-change simulation)

Sofia: filing support tickets for top-3 impacted customers and offering priority repro help.
Jesse: logging TODO: add correlation id in auth-proxy refresh path so we can trace token refresh origins into apigw traces.
Pranav: rolling back edge token-cache? keep it enabled for now, we saw net improvement. will collect hit-rate metrics and revert if issues.
Tom: filing PR for cache warmup strategy (WIP) at https://git.internal/repo/PR-4192
Amanda: final checks: any unresolved customer-impact threads? Sofia: ACME open, assigned to Dana in support, they're happy with current perf.
support-bot: incident ticket created: INC-20260318-1123. severity: high. linked to status page.
Amanda: wrap-up: good triage and fast rollback. we'll draft postmortem and share with Eng + Support. thanks team. :rocket:
Sofia: adding postmortem attendees: Eng-runtime, Eng-platform, SDK, Support, SRE.
Jesse: follow-up sync tomorrow 15:00 UTC to review action progress.
Amanda: closing warroom thread, further updates will be in postmortem doc.
